confidence_note: Book is Atomic Habits (2018). 1.01^365 = 37.78 and 0.99^365 = 0.03 are Clear's own arithmetic (confirmed by summaries). The ice-cube plateau image (a room at 25 degrees Fahrenheit, melting at 32) is in the same chapter; kept brief. Arithmetic is an illustration, not a forecast; real progress is uneven.
facts: Clear writes that if you get 1 percent better each day for a year you end up about 37 times better (1.01 to the 365th is 37.78).
If you get 1 percent worse each day you end up near zero (0.99 to the 365th is 0.03).
Small habits seem to make no difference on a given day.
Results arrive late: the effects of habits compound like interest and show up after a delay.
Clear's ice-cube image: a cube in a cold room (25 degrees F) shows nothing as the room warms to 26, 27, 28; it melts at 32. The work was not wasted.
Caveat: the math is an illustration; real improvement is uneven.
scene_details: An ice cube on a table
tension: Skipping one day changes nothing you can see.
opening_idea: Open on the two numbers 37.78 and 0.03.

lessons.idea: The cost or gain of one day is invisible, so judge the direction you are repeating.
lessons.everyday_example_idea: A cook who keeps tasting as he goes.

reflect_final: Which small thing do you repeat each day that you would not notice for months, in either direction?

use_cases.situation: Someone says one missed workout does not matter.
use_cases.move: Agree about one day, then ask about the trend.
Choose a daily step with the least friction.
Remind yourself of the ice cube.

pocket_idea: One percent a day is 37.78 times in a year on paper and 0.03 the other way; one day shows nothing, the direction shows everything.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: A habit that gets 1 percent better a day multiplies to 37.78; 1 percent worse leaves 0.03.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: Clear: 1% better daily is 37.78x in a year, 1% worse is 0.03. An ice cube melts only at 32 degrees.
